name: Saint Vincent of Saragossa
history: A deacon of Saragossa in Spain who preached for his bishop, Valerius, and was arrested with him in the persecution of Diocletian. While the old bishop was sent into exile, Vincent was tortured at Valencia with savage cruelty and died of his wounds. His fame spread through the whole Church; Saint Augustine preached several sermons on his feast.
life: Vincent served Bishop Valerius of Saragossa as his deacon, and tradition holds that he preached in his place because the bishop found speaking difficult. When the governor Dacian enforced the decrees of Diocletian, both were taken in chains to Valencia. Valerius was exiled; Vincent, who answered for them both, was stretched on the rack, torn with iron hooks and laid on a red-hot grid, yet he remained calm and even joyful. Thrown into a cell strewn with broken pottery, he is said to have converted his jailer. He died soon afterwards. The governor ordered his body left for the beasts, but tradition says a raven guarded it. His relics were later venerated at Valencia and, from the twelfth century, at Lisbon, whose patron he is. In the wine country of France his day is still kept by the growers as their own.
prayerTo: Saint Vincent, deacon and martyr, you spoke for your bishop and suffered for your Lord with a peace no torment could break. Pray for deacons and for all who serve the Church. Pray for me, that in pain and trouble I may keep my trust in Christ and my joy in Him. Amen.
penance: Vincent served the Church as a deacon. Offer some practical help to your parish today, and pray for deacons and those preparing for ordination.
meditation: Augustine said that Vincent conquered both in what he said and in what he suffered. Where does your faith need to show itself less in words and more in endurance?
prayer: Give heed to our humble prayers, O Lord, that we who know we are guilty of our own sin, may be saved by the intercession of Your blessed Martyrs Vincent and Anastasius. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
